newsitem.title: DUBAI: Japan says U.S.to blame for Mideast peace freeze.
newsitem.headline: Japan says U.S.to blame for Mideast peace freeze.

text.p: The United States is to blame for a deadlocked Middle East peace process and should adopt a positive role to revive stalled negotiations, Minoro Tampa, Japan's ambassador to Saudi Arabia said on Sunday.
"The U.S. bias to Israel is what caused the impasse in the peace process," Tampa told news conference in Riyadh marking the end of his term in Saudi Arabia.

"Japan appeals to the U.S. to work seriously towards restoring its role as a sponsor of the peace process and put an end to the current deterioration," he said adding that failure to resolve the Middle East issue was contrary to the interests of many countries.

Talks between Israel and the Palestinians broke down in March when the Jewish state began building a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. The Palestinians want Israel to freeze settlement building before they return to the negotiating table but Israel has so far refused.
Three months of deadlock last week erupted into daily clashes between stone-throwing Arab demonstrators and Israeli troops in the divided West Bank city of Hebron.

The violence erupted after a U.S. congressional vote last week demanded President Bill Clinton recognise Arab East Jerusalem - occupied by Israel in 1967 and revered by Palestinians as the capital of their future state - as part of the capital of the Jewish state.
